verdict.rationale: iTerm2's own docs say it ships a custom escape sequence that displays images, including animated GIFs, directly in the terminal, and the GitHub README repeats this with the imgcat utility. Community users confirm it works hands-on, including across SSH, with a matplotlib backend rendering plots inline, and with base64 data prefixed by the escape sequence. missing for 10: the protocol specification or escape-sequence reference itself is not in the pack (only feature-page mentions), and imgcat is not installed by default, so users must download it separately.

support.subject: As a developer, I can display inline images and rich graphics via a documented terminal graphics protocol

citations.quote: iTerm2 has a custom escape sequence to display images right in the terminal. Even animated GIFs!
Display images (including animated GIFs) directly in the terminal. Use imgcat to view photos, charts, or visual output without leaving your workflow.
imgcat: you can view images without leaving your terminal. Somehow this works even across SSH connections
One user uses a matplotlib backend that renders plots inline, which makes remote work nicer.
